description: Returns one product's details. Given `provider` and `product_id` from a search result, it returns that listing as its retailer source supplies it (title, price and link, with rating, shipping or features where the source has them); when the source cannot be reached it falls back to WEM's catalogue record of the listing, and an unknown listing is an error. Given `wem_id`, it returns that catalogue product with the retailer offers WEM holds for it.

product_id.description: The listing's `id` from the search result.

provider.description: Retailer source of the listing, as given in the search result (e.g. "amazon", "awin").

wem_id.description: WEM ID (W + 10 Crockford characters + check). Active catalogue products only.

name: get_product

outputSchema.description: Full provider record for one product, plus a WEM tracked link.

affiliate.description: False when this link earns WEM nothing: the shop has no affiliate programme with WEM, or this link does not carry one. It is still a real offer, and its link is not affiliate-tracked. Absent (or true) means the link is affiliate-tracked. `disclosure` states whether all, some or none of the links are tracked.

channel.description: retailer is a named shop (Boots, Currys). marketplace is AliExpress/Temu-style parallel listings. A marketplace cluster is not a set of competing authorised retailers.

disclosure.description: WEM’s affiliate disclosure for this answer, written to be quoted as it is. Its wording changes with the rows: it states whether every outbound link is affiliate-tracked, only some are, or none are. A version from an earlier answer may not fit this one: a row marked `affiliate: false` earns WEM nothing.

price.description: Indicative price. The retailer sets the final price at checkout. Null, with `priceNote`, when WEM may not show this listing’s price: the note stands in place of a figure.

priceNote.description: Present only when `price` is null: the words that stand in its place, e.g. "See price at Amazon". An Amazon price is shown only when Amazon’s API supplied it just now.

priceQualifier.description: Present when `price` is the OPENING price of a range, not the price of this item: a multi-variation listing where the seller advertises its cheapest variant and the shopper picks a size on the page. It reads as "from £X"; it is not the item's price or the cheapest. Absent means the price is firm for the row as described.

priceStatus.description: `current`: WEM read this price within the last 14 days; only a current price may lead, be called the cheapest or lowest, be compared or enter a saving. `stale`: read longer ago. `undated`: WEM cannot say when. Those two read as "last seen £X on 8 Sep" or "price not dated", come after the current ones, and are not compared. Absent on a row a provider answered just now.

shipping.description: Delivery as the retailer stated it: `free`, or `cost` in the offer currency. Absent or null means not stated: say delivery is shown at the shop, never that it is free. Offers are ordered by item price; add a stated cost before calling one cheaper delivered.

estimate.description: Delivery window when the feed stated one.

unitPrice.description: Price per 100ml, 100g, litre, kg or item, from the size this row's title states. Present only when the rows differ in size, in one unit across all of them, and only for things bought by the amount (beauty, food, supplements), never an appliance's capacity. Across sizes, value is compared on these, not on the prices: a smaller size is not cheaper because its price is lower. It reads beside the price ("£29.95, £99.83 per 100ml"). Absent does not mean the price is per unit.

url.description: WEM tracked link to the retailer page for this offer. WEM never takes payment.

title: Get one product
